scope.review: Independent first full English fidelity review of D1790 against approved Chinese and the registered 9p Faraday-laws source; not 10p N101.
scope.method: Read the complete source, approved Chinese, English draft, saved English paragraph flow, historical Chinese SCI and freeze, retained text snapshots, and figure evidence JSON. Compare meanings, conditions, references, object identities, ordered math and numeric sequences, and actual file hashes without executing a native validator or re-deriving source science.

objectReviews.assessment: Preserves Faraday's two electrolysis laws and the charge-to-deposited-mass introduction.

Same substance and electrode-reaction conditions, constant current and neglected side reactions govern the first law. Preserves m=kIt=kq, It=q, the one-coulomb numerical definition of k, and the distinction between total and target-reaction charge.
Preserves electrochemical-equivalent SI units kg/C and their mass-to-charge meaning.
Measurement of m and q retains the specified-deposition-reaction and negligible-competing-reaction conditions.
Preserves the ionic charge-transfer explanation and explicitly keeps the same-reaction-conditions premise.

Figure 194 remains the same-electrolyte, same-reaction, equal-time comparison with differing currents, I1=I2+I3, corresponding deposited masses, constant currents and side-reaction controls. No equal-branch-current claim is introduced.

Preserves reaction-specific valence, oppositely signed singly charged K/Br ions, divalent copper and sulfate charge magnitudes, and the warning against modeling dissociation as bare copper atoms losing electrons. KBr illustrates ionic charges, not potassium deposition.
Figure-194 identity and position are preserved. Review covers grouped English context semantics only; source/geometry approval is inherited.
Visible caption Figure 194 faithfully localizes the numbered source caption without adding an apparatus claim.

Preserves n as appropriate to the ion and electrode reaction, A as the source's atomic-weight notation interpreted as molar mass, A/n as chemical equivalent in kg/mol, and its distinction from dimensionless relative atomic mass and particle count.

Figure 195 remains different electrolytes in series, equal current and equal charge over the same time, q=It only for constant current, and masses proportional to respective chemical equivalents under specified reactions and neglected side reactions. Equal deposited masses are expressly denied.
Figure-195 identity and position are preserved. Review covers grouped English context semantics only; source/geometry approval is inherited.
Visible caption Figure 195 faithfully localizes the numbered source caption.

Preserves the fixed-q first-law relation and the additional different-electrolyte experimental comparison needed for the second law. Keeps actual-electrode-reaction valence; does not make the first law alone prove the second.
Preserves the direction of proportionality, coefficient 1/F, k=(1/F)(A/n) and label (10-6).
Faraday constant conveys both Chinese names for the same F; preserves the denial of an arbitrarily electrolyte-dependent material parameter.
Preserves substitution of (10-6) into (10-5), m=(1/F)(A/n)q, label (10-7), and the three quantities related.
Preserves charge per mole of transferred electrons and the specified-unit numerical comparison. Does not identify sample mass with molar mass or coulombs with coulombs per mole.

Preserves Avogadro's identity, valence-adjusted particle-number coefficient in per-mole units, F=q_n(N_A/n), label (10-8), and q_n as charge transferred per corresponding ion in magnitude, not signed ionic charge. Faraday is present in the actual prose as well as entity metadata.
F=96500 C/mol is explicitly the textbook's experimental approximation and rounded calculation value, not an exact modern value.

Preserves copper sulfate, valence 2 and n=2, 0.03177 kg/mol, the numerically corresponding sample mass and 96500 C, the ordered 6.02 and 3.01 times 10^23 coefficient calculation, q_n approximately 3.2 times 10^-19 C, (10-9), per-mole versus actual particle-count distinction, and precision qualifications.

Retains the approved correction that a depositing copper ion gains two electrons, not the raw source's misleading copper-atom dissociation explanation. Preserves e=q_n/2 and the original approximate 1.6 times 10^-19 C to 4.8 times 10^-10 older electrostatic-unit chain; positive magnitude is not positive electron charge.
Preserves Joffe and Millikan, agreement only at the textbook's precision, different measurement methods and the seventh-grade textbook as background, not an assigned task.

Preserves the later electron-charge determination, Faraday's earlier empirical laws and the then-unknown electron and internal atomic/molecular structure. No unsupported historical date or substitute scientist is added.
Preserves aqueous and molten electrolytes and distinguishes ionic transport within the medium from electrode charge transfer linked to deposited mass.

boundaryReviews.assessment: Introduction to first law; its conditions remain immediately before the law statement.
First-law experiment to second-law and ionic-valence discussion.
Definition of F to its physical meaning and substitution.
Rounded F qualification to electron-charge determination.
Charge-sign and historical-unit qualifications to experimental comparison and historical conclusion.

observations.assessment: No English-introduced omission, incorrect scientific identity, altered numerical or mathematical sequence, missing condition, or materially changed conclusion was found in any of the 25 objects or 50 paragraphs. This decision comes from full bilingual/source reading, not solely from native success.

The 96500 value, source coefficient calculation, copper charge approximation and older electrostatic-unit conversion stay explicitly approximate. No modern exact constant, external metrological claim or additional precision has been substituted.

The English retains every substantive Chinese resolution documented by the old SCI: constant-current/common-time/side-reaction premises, molar versus sample mass, per-mole coefficient versus actual count, transferred charge magnitude versus signed ionic charge, copper ions gaining electrons, and the experimental premise needed for the second law. None was re-derived or newly approved as source science.

Faraday, Avogadro, Joffe and Millikan retain corresponding source_term mappings and source-bound reasons. Both Chinese names for F have the same English equivalent, Faraday constant; collapsing those synonymous names does not omit a second physical quantity.
The supplied range 10-5 through 10-9 contains five actual printed equation labels, not four. All five were reviewed and retained.

English object 9 has a bold marker directly after the period ending the relative-atomic-mass sentence, followed by a newline. The chemical-equivalent definition, unit and meaning remain complete. This is a formatting observation, not an English-fidelity defect or rendered-layout approval; no edit was made.

The retained native-flow snapshot contains all 35 matching paragraph texts and candidate adjacent boundaries, but its resolvedBreaks array is empty. The historical freeze and frozen/current lesson section_breaks supply the five selected concept boundaries. This review does not claim that the old snapshot itself recorded five resolved breaks.

limitations: Text-only English fidelity approval for this exact D1790 draft and its implied grouped context. Not source extraction/completeness approval, new SCI, full native finalization, publication, browser/layout acceptance or full-course approval.

No images were visually opened or rendered. SVG bytes were hashed only; inherited figure source/geometry decisions were read from existing evidence and not replayed. Raster source-image hashes remain inherited, not independently recomputed here.

Historical original tmp snapshot paths are no longer present at those locations. Actual retained author-history text files with the exact SCI/freeze hashes provide the bindings recorded above; no absent original path is claimed to have been read.
The freeze's pre-SCI awaiting status is historical author state, not a pass receipt. The separately bound Chinese science-review file is the inherited pass.
No downstream English manifest or newly emitted grouped-context file was reviewed. Protected machine-label restoration is a stipulated technical follow-up, not performed or claimed complete here.

No DB operations, paid generation, browser operations, Git operations, tests, native reruns, asset edits, source edits, other-chat messaging or delegation were performed. The only file written is this review.
conclusion: English fidelity passed for phy9-c2-s4-n101 in 9p, including every object, all 50 semantic paragraphs, five concept boundaries, complete math/numeric ordering and the single grouped figure-context semantics. Inherited Chinese/source SCI is reused through actual source, freeze, retained-template and current-prose bindings; it was not replayed. Existing independent figure source/geometry approval and original SVG bytes are retained.
